newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UNHCR halts Chechen aid after Red Cross murders.
newsitem.headline: UNHCR halts Chechen aid after Red Cross murders.

text.p: The U.N. refugee agency said on Tuesday it had frozen all humanitarian work for 80,000 displaced Chechens in areas neighbouring Chechnya after the killing of six Western Red Cross staffers.

Spokeswoman Maki Shinohara said the UNHCR, which had no staff in Chechnya itself, had halted its work in the neighbouring republics of Dagestan, Ingushetia and North Ossetia for security reasons. U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees Sadako Ogata expressed deep concern at lack of security for aid workers in a Geneva meeting with Russian deputy foreign minister Nikolai Afanasievsky, she said.

The UNHCR spokeswoman told Reuters that emergency aid, sanitation and housing projects carried out by 13 international and 30 local staffers had been put on hold in the turbulent north Caucasus region because of security fears.

The International Committee of the Red Cross froze its work in Chechnya on Tuesday after masked gunmen killed six of its staff members, among them four women, in a dawn attack on a hospital compound in the Chechen village of Novye Atagi.
Shinohara said Ogata expressed deep concern to Afanasievsky over the killings -- the worst assault on ICRC staff and the bloodiest incident involving foreigners on Russian soil for many years.

Tens of thousands of people have been killed in Chechnya since Russia sent troops there in December 1994 to crush an independence bid. The fighting has been punctuated by claims and counter claims about who is responsible for what.
